Subject: Coordinating backup purge windows and evidence handoff

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams reviewed Redwood's standard retention language and we have two items that need operational clarity before we can sign the DPA amendment:

1) Backup purge phasing — we need to understand safe staging windows. Several of our downstream systems replicate nightly snapshots; if Redwood initiates a bulk purge for a delete request, we need a minimal rollback window to surface evidence for an ongoing investigation.

2) Circuit-breaker for rolling deletions — in incident scenarios (e.g., mistaken bulk deletion), do you support a circuit-breaker to pause the purge and isolate affected shards/regions while you extract and escrow evidence? If so, please describe the shortest practical pause and what logs/artifacts you can provide on an expedited basis.

Can you loop in your privacy/compliance folks and send a recommended operational sequence and sample runbook? We prefer a short, bulleted response we can attach to our legal note.

Thanks,
Alice Tan
Head of Security Programs
MediCorp Health

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers below; attaching a short diagram and a draft DPA clause we usually propose for these cases.

Summary (short):
- Rolling purge can be staged by region and snapshot generation time; customers can opt for a 72-hour staging window by default or tighten to 24 hours for sensitive classes.
- We support an automated "circuit-breaker" that halts further purge jobs for a customer scope and creates an immutable forensic bundle (KV cache snapshot + ingestion logs + purge manifest).
- For expedited evidence requests we can deliver the forensic bundle within 24 hours (SLA-tier dependent) and retain the bundle in a secure escrow for 30 days.

Proposed operational sequence (recommended):
1) Customer initiates deletion request -> Redwood flags objects and creates purge manifest.
2) Staging window (configurable): default 72h; customer may request 24h for high-risk workloads. During staging we do not remove backups that fall into the staging epoch.
3) Circuit-breaker option: customer or Redwood operator can trigger pause; we mark affected shards read-only for purge jobs and snapshot current KV caches.
4) Forensic bundle assembly: logs (access, ingestion, purge attempts), snapshot checksums, and a signed purge manifest. Bundle packaged and checksum-stamped.
5) Delivery/escrow: via encrypted S3 link or signed transfer to customer KMS; optionally push to third-party escrow (legal team).

Operational notes:
- Cross-border transfers: if evidence contains EU/UK-personal data, transfer follows customer-selected transfer mechanism (SCCs or approved transfer contract).
- Subprocessor involvement: backups stored with subprocessor partners are subject to subproc SLA; we can coordinate on expedited retrieval but timelines vary.

Attaching: redwood-backup-phasing-diagram.pdf; dpa-backup-amendment-draft.docx

Let us know preferred staging window and whether you need the forensic bundle escrowed to a neutral third party.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Alice/Karthik — adding operational constraints from compliance/runtime side. Short bullets:

- Log retention exceptions: we can mark a short-term exception to preserve internal op-logs and request traces for up to 90 days beyond standard retention exclusively for forensic bundles; exceptions must be scoped to the customer and timeboxed.

- Minimum pause window: while the circuit-breaker can be triggered immediately, practical isolation to guarantee bundle consistency requires a 4-hour quiesce for high-ingest shards and up to 12 hours for long-tail archival merges (we'll accelerate where possible).

- Evidence contents: ingestion deltas, internal audit trail (who initiated/approved), replication manifests, and snapshot checksums. We cannot include third-party tenant data in any bundle.

- Crossborder & subprocessors: if backups are replicated to a subprocessor region, we need written approval to pull evidence; our runbook includes an "expedite subproc retrieval" checkbox that triggers partner SLAs (typ. 24–72h).

Next steps: if MediCorp agrees to either 72h or 24h staging, we will produce a redline to the DPA clause KPI and add a contract-level circuit-breaker acceptance. Otherwise, procurement/legal needs to approve longer staging.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Alice — a few legal/contract items to keep this tidy for procurement:

- We will add an addendum that defines the staging window (customer-selectable: 24h/72h) and the circuit-breaker procedure. The addendum will expressly state the scope of the forensic bundle and the escrow duration (30 days by default).

- Subprocessor retrieval: clause will require customer authorization before Redwood requests evidence from a subprocessor if the data resides outside Redwood-controlled systems. This prevents surprise crossborder pulls.

- SLA and fees: expedited forensic bundles (<24h) fall under an incident response add-on; we will include standard and expedited tiers in the DPA amendment. Please flag if Medicorp needs expedited tier as part of initial onboarding.

- Evidence transfer and KMS: we will include an option for transfer encrypted with Medicorp's KMS key.

If you confirm the staging window preference and whether you want escrow to a neutral third party, I'll circulate the redline for signature (DocuSign).
